Do not begin or end the Ramadan fast until the new moon is seen, and if it is cloudy, calculate thirty days; the month may also have twenty-nine.
Showing ten, ten and nine with his fingers, the Prophet taught that a month may be twenty-nine days, adding that his people are unlettered, neither writing nor counting.
Begin the fast on sighting the new moon and end it on sighting the next, and if clouds hide it, complete thirty days.
Having sworn to stay away from his wives for a month, the Prophet returned after twenty-nine days, saying a month may be twenty-nine, as he showed with his fingers.
Ibn Abbas kept to Medina's sighting rather than Syria's, saying the month counts from when the moon is seen; the months of Eid, Ramadan and Dhu'l-Hijja, are not incomplete.
